questions.text: What is the best source-backed definition of Bahay na Bato?

options.text: A hybrid house type combining indigenous and Hispanic traditions, built partly of wood and partly of stone.
A purely modern steel office tower without domestic planning.
A pre-colonial boat-house with no Hispanic influence.
A utility code term for water service entrance.

questions.rationale: A hybrid house type combining indigenous and Hispanic traditions, built partly of wood and partly of stone. HOA Module 4 P1 describes Bahay na Bato and arquitectura mestiza as hybrid construction.
questions.explanation: The volada (literally 'thrown out' in Spanish) is a defining feature of the bahay na bato's upper floor. It is a cantilevered wooden balcony that projects outward beyond the masonry wall line of the ground floor — an engineering feat using timber brackets and balaustre (turned wooden balusters). Functionally, it shades the zaguan/silung below from sun and rain (extending the climate-responsive bahay kubo logic to the colonial hybrid), and provides outdoor living/social space for the household on the upper level.

questions.rationale: A hybrid house type combining indigenous and Hispanic traditions, built partly of wood and partly of stone. HOA Module 4 P1 describes Bahay na Bato and arquitectura mestiza as hybrid construction.
questions.explanation: The bahay na bato is a true hybrid: (1) AUSTRONESIAN heritage: The raised upper floor on a stone base preserves the bahay kubo's fundamental climate logic — elevating the living space above flood level and allowing air circulation under the floor. The capiz-shell window panels (ventanillas) continue the bahay kubo's tradition of open, ventilating walls. (2) SPANISH contribution: Stone and masonry construction on the ground floor, formal room names (sala, comedor, cocina), and decorative elements. The genius of arquitectura mestiza is that the Spanish colonists accepted the raised-floor logic because it worked in the tropical seismic environment, while adding stone construction for durability and status.
